preconditions.description: The lower bound l is an integer between 1 and 10^800 inclusive.
The upper bound r is an integer between l and 10^800 inclusive.
The length n of the string is an integer between 1 and 2000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(sub) <= int(r) for sub in [s[i:j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n+1) if s[i] != '0'])
postconditions.description: All non-empty substrings of the output string s, without leading zeros, are modest integers.
The output string s has length n.

postconditions.expression: count == sum(1 for sub in [s[i:j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n+1) if s[i] != '0'] if int(l) <= int(sub) <= int(r))
postconditions.description: The count is the number of modest substrings in the output string s.

postconditions.expression: all(s[i] in '0123456789' for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The output string s consists only of digits.

postconditions.expression: all(s[i] <= s[i+1] for i in range(n-1) if s[i] != '0' and s[i+1] != '0') or s == min([s for s in [str(i) for i in range(10**n)] if all(1 <= int(sub) <= int(r) for sub in [s[i:j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n+1) if s[i] != '0'])], key=lambda x: (sum(1 for sub in [x[i:j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n+1) if x[i] != '0'] if int(l) <= int(sub) <= int(r)), x))
postconditions.description: The output string s is the lexicographically smallest string among all strings of length n with the maximum number of modest substrings.
